chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddaq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

He was asked about a man who performs wudu (ablution) and then touches the inner part of his anus. He said: his wudu (ablution) is invalidated. And if he touches the inside of his urethral opening, then he must repeat the wudu (ablution). And if he is in salat (prayer), he should break the salat (prayer), perform wudu (ablution), and repeat the salat (prayer). And if he opens his urethral opening, he repeats the wudu (ablution) and repeats the salat (prayer).

So the proper way regarding this report is that we interpret it to mean that if he encounters some najasah (ritual impurity) there, then repeating the wudu (ablution) and the salat (prayer) becomes obligatory upon him at that time. But whenever he does not encounter any such thing, then nothing is upon him, according to what we have stated previously.

key_terms.النَّجَاسَةِ: ritual impurity present in the area
key_terms.بَاطِنَ دُبُرِهِ: the inner part of his anus

ai.seo_question: Does touching the private parts after wudu (ablution) invalidate wudu (ablution) in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses rulings concerning touching the internal parts of the private passages after wudu (ablution), and its apparent effect on wudu (ablution) and salat (prayer). The concluding statement explains that the report is to be understood in the case where najasah (ritual impurity) is present; otherwise, no obligation is incurred.
